clue.text: Women's Institute has new department to clean up national skin condition

parts.note: WI is the standard abbreviation for the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
N is the abbreviation for new
D is a common abbreviation for department

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to rub something is to clean or polish it
N is the abbreviation for national

explanation.surface: A WI member and a government department set out to tackle a skin complaint affecting the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National skin condition' reads as one phrase, but national only supplies its abbreviation and the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Windburn is the reddened, sore skin caused by exposure to strong wind, a recognised skin complaint.

clue.text: Main fastener

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a basic, principal item
second meaning: a bent wire clip that holds sheets of paper together

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like the chief fastener; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means chief or principal, and as a noun it is a small wire clip for binding paper.

clue.text: About to listen to beginning and end of scripture read aloud?

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning
to hear is to listen to

indicators.note: beginning and end asks for only the first and last letters of the word that follows

parts.note: the first and last letters of scripture

explanation.surface: A reader is about to hear the opening and close of a scripture passage read out in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that reading lines aloud is only one kind of rehearsal, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors rehearse by speaking their lines through in practice, so running through a text out loud is one form of it.

clue.text: Chicken in bar upset mouse's resting place

parts.note: to bar something is to ban it

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a computer mouse rests on a mouse mat

explanation.surface: A chicken loose in a pub knocks over the spot where the mouse sleeps.
explanation.walkthrough: The mouse is a computer mouse, not a rodent; its resting place is the mat it sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic chicken.

clue.text: Intimate in well finds religion

indicators.note: in says one word sits inside the other

parts.note: so and well are both interjections used to start a remark
to intimate is to hint

explanation.surface: Someone peering down a well, or deep within themselves, comes upon faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Intimate looks like an adjective meaning close, but it is the verb meaning to suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan, centred on the worship of kami spirits.

clue.text: Proverbial glutton entertained by drunkard offering bung

indicators.note: something entertained by a host is held inside it, as a guest is in a house

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
to eat like a pig is the proverbial image of gluttony

explanation.surface: A greedy eater is fed by a drunk who offers him a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: Bung is British slang for a bribe, which fits the surface, but here it is the stopper of a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or plug used to stop the vent hole of a cask, the same thing as a bung.

clue.text: Take oriental food — not a meal!

indicators.note: not a tells us to drop a letter A from the word just before

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, as on old prescriptions
E is the abbreviation for east, so oriental
pasta is an Italian staple food

explanation.surface: An order for Asian takeaway, with the cheeky insistence that it isn't a proper meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes the definition look like a denial, but meal is the definition and not a is the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or literary word for a meal.

clue.text: Squeeze queen into skimpy garment

indicators.note: into says one piece is squeezed inside another

parts.note: a thong is a very skimpy item of underwear or swimwear
R stands for rex or regina, so queen

explanation.surface: A monarch tries to wriggle into a scanty piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Squeeze looks like the container signal, but it is the definition: a noun meaning a crush of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeeze can mean a crowded crush of people, which is exactly what a throng is.

clue.text: Sedentary character's disgruntled pooch out with cat

indicators.note: a disgruntled creature is out of sorts, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lazy pet owner's grumpy dog has been put out alongside the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch potato is an idiom for someone who lounges on the sofa doing little but watching television.

clue.text: Party in Ireland after victory's end

parts.note: a win is a victory
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A celebration in Ireland once a victory has been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the party second: victory comes first. The DUP is a political party in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind-up is the conclusion or final stage of something, so an ending.

clue.text: Upset by bowling spell: time that is used to keep the Ashes

parts.note: in cricket an over is a spell of six balls from one bowler
T is the abbreviation for time

parts.words: that is used to keep the Ashes
parts.note: cricket's Ashes trophy is a tiny urn

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator's line about a spell of bowling that lets England keep the Ashes series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia, whose trophy is a small urn said to hold burnt bails.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to upset, in the sense of knocking something over or reversing a decision.

clue.text: One leaving marriage rejected as socially unacceptable

indicators.note: rejected suggests sent back, so the remaining letters are read backwards
something leaving goes away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a marriage is a union
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone walking out of a marriage is shunned as beyond the pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U, from 'not upper class', was the 1950s label for speech and habits judged unrefined by the British upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U describes manners thought not to belong to the upper class, hence socially unacceptable in snobbish eyes.

clue.text: Ten campers blown over cliff

indicators.note: things blown over by the wind are scattered and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A storm sweeps a party of ten campers off a clifftop.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarpment is a long steep slope or cliff, typically at the edge of a plateau.

clue.text: Devious tarts with pen catching blokes in stings

indicators.note: catching says the outer letters trap another piece inside them
devious means winding and indirect, so the letters take a twisted route into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: Scheming women of the night with a writer lure men into police stings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stings are police undercover operations that lure suspects into crime, which is entrapment.

clue.text: Transfer idiot in government

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule or government
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A call to move a fool out of a ministerial post.
explanation.walkthrough: Reign is government in the sense of a monarch's period of rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassign is to transfer someone to a different post or task.

clue.text: Casual worker with sorry tale: the shape of things to come?

definitions.text: the shape of things to come?

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker

indicators.note: sorry means in a poor state, so the letters are in a sorry mess

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A temporary worker with a hard-luck story asks what the future holds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on H. G. Wells's novel title The Shape of Things to Come; the question mark signals the playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern used to cut out or shape items made later, so literally it fixes the shape of future things.

clue.text: Makers of loud noise don't start troubles

indicators.note: don't start tells us to remove the first letter

parts.note: Tannoy is a British brand name for public-address loudspeakers

explanation.surface: Noisy people who won't stop causing problems.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tannoy is the public-address system heard in British stations and schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoys and troubles are both verbs meaning bothers or irritates.

clue.text: Close up, keeping one and six for priest

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
keeping means holding on to something inside

parts.note: a close is an end
I is the Roman numeral for one
VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: Come nearer, holding one and six as payment for the priest.
explanation.walkthrough: Close up reads as a phrase meaning shut, but close is the noun meaning end and up is a separate signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A divine is an old-fashioned noun for a clergyman or theologian.

clue.text: Excited parent with a small belly before birth

indicators.note: an excited state is agitated, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
tum is a child's short word for tummy or belly

explanation.surface: An expectant parent with a little bump, thrilled before the baby arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Antepartum is a medical term for the period preceding childbirth, from Latin ante, before, and partus, birth.

clue.text: English setter with endless credit — it makes one sick

indicators.note: endless means losing its final letter

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the setter refers to themself as me
on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: An English dog that has run up endless debts becomes sickening.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter looks like the dog breed, but it is the crossword's compiler, so ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance given to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Fool has money on horse (favourite)

parts.note: M is a common abbreviation for money
in racing a jockey who is riding is said to be up
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A mug puts his cash on the favourite at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests betting on the favourite, but favourite is a separate piece and on horse means riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Muppet is British slang for a fool or incompetent person, from the TV puppets.

clue.text: Key state out East

indicators.note: out means a letter is put out of the word

parts.note: Maine is a US state
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: The most important US state lies far over in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Key and main are both adjectives meaning chief or most important.

clue.text: County most sloppy about language

indicators.note: about means going around something else
something sloppy is careless and messy, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
Erse is an old name for Irish or Scottish Gaelic

explanation.surface: A remark that one English county is the worst for slovenly speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is one of the counties of England, so it is an example of a county.

clue.text: Weak bad back protected by cushion

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed and shielded within it

parts.note: a pad is a cushion

indicators.note: back means the word runs backwards

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A sufferer with a weak, bad back is propped up on a cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad back' reads as a medical complaint, but back is the reversal signal for bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid means pale and lacking vigour, hence weak or feeble.

clue.text: Tight artist's out of fish

indicators.note: out of means taken away from inside the following word

parts.note: a stingray is a flat fish
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A drunk painter has run out of fish to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight looks like slang for drunk, which fits the artist, but here it means mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal for miserly, which is what stingy means.

clue.text: Insect, let loose, swallowed by another

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower

parts.note: another insect, here a bee

indicators.note: let loose means set free, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect is released, only to be eaten by a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: Another means another insect, following on from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect with hardened wing cases.
